sessions.title: Choose the admitted time label for the shown active form

steps.title: Distinguish active past and present descriptions
steps.body: An active participle describes an entity performing the action. The retained чита́вшая is the past reading form; чита́ющая is the present reading form. The labels in the past and in the present distinguish these supplied forms. They do not identify a passive entity being read. An English description of reading can express the action without itself specifying this past/present contrast.

steps.title: Read the question as well as the form
steps.body: For чита́ющая, select in the present when asked for its time label. For чита́вшая, select in the past for its own time label. Classify the displayed form itself. Selecting the other time label would test following a reversal instruction rather than interpreting the participle. The gloss that read gives an action meaning rather than the requested time classification.

steps.title: Recognize the separate living example
steps.body: The retained живу́щие means living. In the supplied example, people perform the living action; this is an active present participle. Its time classification is in the present, while living is its lexical meaning. This is recognition of the admitted example, not a general algorithm for generating participles of unfamiliar verbs. Interpreting an isolated form does not establish the complete tense or actor of a sentence that has not been supplied.

sessions.title: Distinguish admitted long, short and invariant adjective forms

steps.title: Recognize the long and short forms
steps.body: The retained но́вый and нов both mean new. The first is the long form and the second is the masculine singular short form. The grammatical check asks which form is shown, rather than its English gloss. Long adjectives have case, gender and number inflection; short adjectives vary for gender and number, not case. The retained examples are recognition targets, not a universal rule for producing short forms by removing endings.

steps.title: Distinguish a predicate from a noun description
steps.body: In the taught modern use, short adjectives occur only in the nominative and are used predicatively to describe their subject. A long adjective can modify a noun attributively and can also be a predicate. The choice depends on the sentence, not a universal rule about one fixed word position. The following supplied forms, complete clauses and noun phrases support bounded agreement and function checks; they do not settle every long-versus-short semantic or stylistic choice.

steps.title: A short-looking word need not be a short adjective
steps.body: The retained беж means beige and is an invariant colour form, unchanged for case, gender and number. Its short appearance does not make it the short counterpart of но́вый. Keep lexical meaning, inflection and adjective function separate. The correct glosses remain in Vocabulary Lab as word-meaning practice; they do not satisfy the independent adjective grammar checks.

steps.title: Apply short-form gender and number agreement
steps.body: The supplied short forms of new are нов for masculine singular, нова́ for feminine singular, но́во for neuter singular and новы́ for plural. Short adjectives agree with their subject in gender and number; they do not have a modern case paradigm. In the retained noun examples, книга is feminine singular, письмо is neuter singular, and книги has the supplied plural reading. Choose the short form for that subject rather than another form with the same lexical meaning. Some adjectives lack short forms and stress can change; these supplied forms are not a universal truncation recipe.

steps.title: A long form can be a predicate
steps.body: The complete clauses Поезд старый and Студент новый say that the train is old and the student is new. Their long adjectives predicate a property of the subject. No overt present copula appears in these supplied clauses. Long form therefore does not force attributive function, and a temporary-versus-permanent slogan does not decide every form choice. Read the whole example and its supplied meaning rather than its adjective ending alone.

steps.title: Distinguish a noun phrase from a predication
steps.body: The supplied новый карандаш and новое письмо mean new pencil and new letter. Each is an attributive noun phrase: the adjective modifies the head noun. These phrases alone do not assert that a pencil or letter is new in a complete clause. The adjective and noun agree in gender and number in the supplied singular examples. Do not infer an exceptionless word-position rule or every possible case from an isolated phrase. These exercises assess bounded agreement and function recognition, not unrestricted production or every long/short meaning distinction.

sessions.title: Choose the admitted label for the shown adverbial line

steps.title: Compare two ways of expressing the same sequence
steps.body: The supplied Пообедав, я пошёл гулять means Having eaten, I went for a walk. The opening verbal adverb presents eating before the walking action. The supplied Я пообедал и пошёл гулять gives the sequence with finite verbs joined together. Both describe the same person eating and then going for a walk; they differ in expression.

steps.title: Separate register labels from event meaning
steps.body: In this retained source comparison the verbal-adverb version is labelled bookish speech and the finite-verb version colloquial language. Those labels describe the contrasted register; Having eaten, I went for a walk is the event meaning rather than a register label. A sentence appearing on paper is not automatically bookish, and this pair does not license labelling every verbal adverb in every context as bookish.

sessions.title: Decide comma boundaries in the supplied participial constructions

steps.title: A following descriptive phrase is set off on both sides
steps.body: In Программа, написанная в спешке, выполнила недопустимую операцию. The phrase describing the program follows its noun and is set off by commas on both sides. The retained label выделяется запятыми с двух сторон names that treatment. A single comma before the phrase would omit its closing boundary in this supplied sentence.

steps.title: Compare the phrase placed before its noun
steps.body: In Написанная в спешке программа выполнила недопустимую операцию. The same descriptive phrase precedes the noun. The supplied example has no separating commas: запятые не ставятся is its label. Phrase position helps distinguish these two examples; this does not mean commas are never used before a described noun.

steps.title: Apply the pronoun and cause exceptions
steps.body: The retained rule states exceptions when the described entity is a personal pronoun or the participial phrase expresses a cause. Воспитанный в традициях Фоппы, Бернардо Дзенале и Амброджо Бергоньоне, он прошёл обучение в мастерской Леонардо. The opening phrase describes он, so A separating comma follows the opening participial phrase before the main clause. The comma after Фоппы is internal to the list of names. The later comma after Бергоньоне marks the modifier boundary before он; do not treat every visible comma as a modifier boundary. Изумлённый этим хохотом, Павел сел на пол и смотрел куда-то в угол The retained source row explicitly gives this example a causal shade, so A separating comma follows the opening participial phrase before the main clause. The ordinary preceding-noun label запятые не ставятся cannot cancel these exceptions. The optional source wording личным местоимением and кроме тех случаев identifies a category/connective, not a complete comma decision; its reference question does not satisfy these language checks.

steps.title: Check the continuing clause and sentence end
steps.body: Туча, нависшая над высокими вершинами тополей, уже сыпала дождиком The phrase describes Туча and is followed by the continuing predicate, so Separating commas mark both boundaries of the participial phrase before the sentence continues. Вдали виднеется маяк, стоящий у моря Here the phrase describes маяк and ends the supplied construction, so A separating comma precedes the terminal participial phrase, with no closing comma at sentence end. A closing separating comma would have no continuing clause after it. By contrast, No separating comma is used between the participial phrase and the word it describes. is the ordinary non-causal, non-pronoun preceding-noun default shown in the earlier program example. These are bounded supplied constructions; not every phrase before a noun needs a comma and not every phrase after a word fits one universal rule.

sessions.title: In this admitted pair, the adverbial opening is the bookish option and the finite coordination is the ordinary option.

steps.title: Contrast the adverbial opening with finite coordination
steps.body: In Закончив письмо, Анна пошла на почту., finishing the letter is expressed by the opening verbal adverb. In Анна закончила письмо и пошла на почту., the actions are expressed by coordinated finite verbs. The adverbial opening is the bookish option and the finite coordination the ordinary option in this admitted pair. Both describe finishing before going to the post office; the register choice does not reverse those events.

steps.title: Keep the register claim inside this particular pair
steps.body: The supplied Написанное письмо лежит на столе. contains a passive description and is outside this adverbial-versus-finite pair. Mere appearance in writing also does not establish this bookish classification. A verbal adverb in a different sentence needs its own contextual evidence: this pair does not license every adverbial as bookish. Recognizing the opening word is different from interpreting the whole sentence or judging an unfamiliar style.

sessions.title: Read the passage for the actions, not for whether the style is bookish.

steps.title: Follow the actor and the order of actions
steps.body: In Закончив письмо, Анна пошла на почту и отправила его., Anna finishes the letter before going to the post office and sending it. Anna performs the actions; the letter does not travel alone and the post office does not write it. The finishing phrase belongs before the departure, not after the sending. Read the entire supplied passage when a check shows only a fragment.

steps.title: Resolve the final action without substituting a register answer
steps.body: The supplied отправила его means she sent it, with the letter as the object in this passage. The passage places the sending after Anna goes to the post office. It does not say that she stayed at the table, finished at the market, left the letter at home or received a letter at home. Those alternatives replace a stated event or location. Bookish register classification is a separate objective and cannot answer who acted, where she went or what she did with the letter.

steps.body: The retained СССР corresponds to USSR and is grammatically masculine in the supplied noun use. США corresponds to USA and is grammatically plural. The source lists both as indeclinable: their written forms do not gain case endings in this taught use. An adjective agreeing with the initialism follows the supplied gender or number even though the initialism itself stays unchanged. steps.title: A heading describes the group rather than one country

Abbreviations is a reference heading, not the English gloss of either country example. The optional heading question is reference literacy and cannot satisfy the language checks.

The source lists both as indeclinable: their written forms do not gain case endings in this taught use. An adjective agreeing with the initialism follows the supplied gender or number even though the initialism itself stays unchanged. These examples do not classify every Russian abbreviation or demonstrate spoken pronunciation.

steps.body: The supplied Пусть он читает expresses let him read, and Да будет мир! expresses let there be peace. steps.title: Read the possibility meaning of the supplied conditional forms
steps.body: The retained читал бы and читали бы are grouped under предположительность или возможность, supposition or possibility. The particle combines with the supplied verb form to present a conditional or hypothetical meaning; the past-shaped form alone should not make this a report of an actual completed reading event. An English translation using would depends on context.

sessions.title: Answer from the admitted capstone story

steps.title: Follow the rescue before the second return
steps.body: In the retained story a woman reports that a two-year-old girl remains in the burning house. Bob, the dog sent by the firefighters, returns carrying the girl. The supplied нёс де́вочку belongs to that rescue, before the later discovery involving a doll. The mother is glad her daughter is alive; the passage does not describe the rescue itself as the comic discovery.

steps.title: Connect the laughter to what the dog carries next
steps.body: After the rescue Bob goes back into the house and returns carrying a large doll, expressed by несла́ большу́ю ку́клу. When the people recognize it, все расхохота́лись describes their laughter. The female grammatical form refers to the dog in that part of the narration, not the rescued girl carrying the doll. Match the reaction to the doll discovery and keep the earlier rescue separate. These checks interpret the supplied story, not an unfamiliar passage.

steps.title: Use headword forms and sense together
steps.body: The retained entry for стол identifies a noun, gives стол, стола, столу, столом, столе as forms and states the sense a piece of furniture with a flat top. The form row helps locate the entry; it does not by itself state the sense without the sense field.

Use the sense field to distinguish стоит from the furniture noun. The label сущ. identifies a part of speech; it does not state the furniture sense.
